captions: Pairs trading compares two related series.

The algo measures their spread, then a z-score
describes

how unusual that spread is against its recent
history.
A rule may act when the absolute z-score exceeds
two.
It goes long one leg and short the other,
expecting the relationship to normalize.
The chart is illustrative synthetic data.
The real danger is a broken relationship.

A sector shock, company event, or changing business
model
can make yesterday's pair irrelevant.
A pair is not safe merely because it has
moved together before.

The model needs synchronized data, a clear hedge
rule,
and a way to exit when the spread keeps
widening.
Neutral-looking positions still carry risk.

Opening-range breakout defines a first trading
window.
Its high and low become boundaries.
If price crosses above the high, a long rule
may activate.
If it crosses below the low, a short rule
may activate.
A stop defines failure before the order is sent.
The chart is illustrative synthetic data.

Opening noise, headline gaps, and false breakouts
are the
core danger.
A boundary crossed once is not a guaranteed trend.
A breakout rule must decide its range before the
break.
It must decide its stop before the entry.

Otherwise the system is just reacting after the
emotional
part of the move has arrived.
